- person:harka-sampang.profile: 'Mayor of Dharan from 23 May 2022 to 19 January 2026, elected as an independent; founder of the Shram Sanskriti Party; won Sunsari-1 in 2026. Youths outside the headquarters chanted his name as a preferred interim PM (Setopati). Shortlisted in the Gen Z Discord poll (Al Jazeera). Onlinekhabar reported on 11 September that he supported Karki; Setopati quoted him on 10 September saying "Who am I to agree or disagree?".' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:durga-prasai.roles: ['business', 'activist'] vs ['other'] (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:durga-prasai.profile: 'Medical entrepreneur and political activist. Reporting names him as the chief coordinator of the 28 March 2025 pro-monarchy protest at Tinkune; he was arrested in Bhadrapur, Jhapa, on 11 April 2025 on charges of crimes against the state and organised crime. The name is also printed as Prasain in Kantipur.' vs 'Named in reporting as one of the stakeholders the army chief asked Gen Z groups to talk to on 10 September 2025; Gen Z representatives rejected this. Onlinekhabar (11 September) says Prasai said he would accept whoever leads the government if it provides a way forward. The Kathmandu Post spells the name Prasain.' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:anil-kumar-sinha.profile: 'Former Supreme Court justice (1 August 2016-31 October 2023). Minister in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 to 27 March 2026, holding law, justice and parliamentary affairs and several other portfolios.' vs 'Former Supreme Court justice. Recommended on 21 September 2025 for three portfolios in the Karki cabinet: Industry, Commerce and Supply; Law and Justice; Land Reforms, Cooperatives and Poverty Alleviation.' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:mahabir-pun.profile: 'Technologist and social entrepreneur. Minister of Education, Science and Technology in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 until he resigned on 20 January 2026 to contest the election. Won Myagdi-1 as an independent in March 2026 and was assigned the science, technology and innovation portfolio on 9 June 2026 (ShareSansar).' vs 'Magsaysay Award winner who leads the National Innovation Centre. Shortlisted in the Gen Z Discord poll; named on 21 September 2025 as minister for education and science and technology.' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:mahabir-pun.public_status: 'public-official' vs 'public-figure' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:jagdish-kharel.profile: 'Minister of Communication and Information Technology in the Karki interim government from 22 September 2025 to 19 January 2026, succeeding Prithvi Subba Gurung; member of the House for Lalitpur 2 since 26 March 2026.' vs 'Head of news at Image Media Group and named on 21 September 2025 as information and communications minister in the Karki cabinet (ANI describes him as editor of Image Channels).' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:hanaa-singer-hamdy.profile: 'UN Resident Coordinator in Nepal. - person:gauri-bahadur-karki.profile: 'Retired Supreme Court judge who chaired the commission that investigated the killings and damage of 8-9 September 2025; he handed its report to Prime Minister Sushila Karki (Kathmandu Post, 8 March 2026).' vs 'Former chair of the Special Court; named on 21 September 2025 to lead the judicial inquiry commission on the 8-9 September events. ANI prints the surname as "Kaki".' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:sushila-karki.profile: 'Former Chief Justice of Nepal (acting from 11 July 2016, retired June 2017). Sworn in as interim Prime Minister on 12 September 2025 and held the office until 27 March 2026; the first woman to be Prime Minister. Wikipedia reports that Gen Z organisers selected her name in an online Discord poll. The House of Representatives was dissolved on 12 September 2025 and elections were set for 5 March 2026. On 8 March 2026 she received the report of the commission headed by Gauri Bahadur Karki.' vs 'Transition, 10-14 Sept 2025: proposed by Gen Z groups after a Discord debate on 10 Sept and backed by Mayor Balen Shah; appointed interim prime minister by President Paudel on 12 Sept and sworn in that evening (scheduled 9 pm), the first woman to head the government; took charge at Singha Durbar on 14 Sept and pledged to hand over within six months. Her appointment as a non-member of the House and a former chief justice is challenged as unconstitutional (Articles 76 and 132).' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:kulman-ghising.roles: ['minister', 'other'] vs ['minister'] (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:kulman-ghising.profile: 'Managing director of the Nepal Electricity Authority 2016-2020 and 2021 until his removal on 24 March 2025. Sworn in on 15 September 2025 as minister of energy, water resources and irrigation, also holding urban development and physical infrastructure in the Karki interim government; resigned 7 January 2026. Chairman of the Ujyaalo Nepal Party from 10 January 2026. Wikipedia lists him among the candidates discussed for interim prime minister.' vs 'Transition, 10-14 Sept 2025: former head of the Nepal Electricity Authority, one of the names raised in the Discord debate and in press reports as a possible interim PM (reports conflict on whether he was a live candidate); sworn in on 15 Sept as minister for energy, water resources and irrigation with infrastructure and transport and urban development.' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:om-prakash-aryal.profile: 'Advocate. Sworn in on 15 September 2025 as Minister of Home Affairs in the Karki interim government, also holding law, justice and parliamentary affairs until 22 September 2025. Home Minister until 26 March 2026; succeeded by Sudan Gurung.' vs 'Transition, 10-14 Sept 2025: lawyer and former legal adviser to the Kathmandu mayor who coordinated with Karki and took part in the talks with the President; sworn in on 15 Sept as home minister and minister for law, justice and parliamentary affairs. Sudan Gurung\'s group accused him on 14 Sept of "making himself home minister from inside".' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:rameshwor-khanal.profile: "Sworn in on 15 September 2025 as finance minister in the Karki interim government at Shital Niwas. The Kathmandu Post spells his name 'Rameshore Khanal'; the Karki cabinet page on Wikipedia lists 'Rameshwar Khanal' as finance minister until 27 March 2026." vs 'Transition, 10-14 Sept 2025: former finance secretary who chaired the High-Level Economic Reform Recommendation Commission; sworn in on 15 Sept as finance minister. Spelled Rameshore Khanal by the Kathmandu Post and Tribune.' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:sudan-gurung.profile: 'Founder of Hami Nepal, the youth NGO that called the 8 September 2025 protest and, per Wikipedia, liaised between organisers and the Nepali Army afterwards. Joined the RSP on 18 January 2026, won Gorkha 1 on 9 March 2026, became Home Minister on 27 March 2026, resigned on 22 April 2026 citing moral responsibility amid a controversy over his financial conduct, and was reappointed on 9 June 2026 after an inquiry cleared him (ShareSansar, Wikipedia). The Ministry of Home Affairs website names him as minister (accessed 2026-10-05; Nepali spelling there: Sudhan Gurung).' vs 'Transition, 10-14 Sept 2025: founder of Hami Nepal and chief negotiator for the Gen Z side with the army chief and President; told reporters on 11 Sept that the first demand was dissolution of parliament; reportedly insisted on dissolution first on 12 Sept; his team was reported meeting on key government posts on 14 Sept, while Hami Nepal leaders were also reported as refusing to join the government; on the night of 14 Sept his group protested at Baluwatar against the cabinet expansion.' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:balendra-shah.profile: "Known as Balen. Elected Mayor of Kathmandu as an independent in May 2022; resigned on 18 January 2026 to contest the 5 March 2026 election. Joined the Rastriya Swatantra Party (from 28 December 2025 per Wikipedia), won Jhapa 5 defeating KP Sharma Oli, and was sworn in as Prime Minister on 27 March 2026. The Ministry of Defence and the Prime Minister's Office websites list him as Prime Minister (accessed 2026-10-05)." vs 'Transition, 10-14 Sept 2025: Kathmandu mayor. Backed Karki on Facebook (reported as Wednesday 10 Sept by ANI; after the 11 Sept nomination by the Kathmandu Post); popular with some youth groups outside Army Headquarters who chanted his name; reported as having declined an interim role (Nepali Times) or being unreachable by the Discord moderators (Al Jazeera).' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:ram-chandra-paudel.profile: 'President of Nepal since 13 March 2023, succeeding Bidya Devi Bhandari. Member of the Nepali Congress until 2023, then left active party membership after the presidential election (Wikipedia). Earlier Speaker of the House of Representatives (1994-1999), Deputy Prime Minister and Home Minister (2000-2001). In September 2025 he administered the oath to the Karki interim ministers at Shital Niwas.' vs "Transition, 10-14 Sept 2025: coordinated with Army Chief Sigdel the talks with Gen Z, consulted party leaders and constitutional experts, reportedly resisted dissolving parliament before conceding on 12 Sept; announced Karki's appointment, dissolved the House of Representatives from 11 pm and set elections for 5 March 2026. Nepali Times reports he was criticised for being sidelined by the army (single account)." (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:ashok-raj-sigdel.profile: "Chief of the Army Staff since 9 September 2024; appointed on the Council of Ministers' recommendation and announced on 28 August 2024, succeeding Prabhu Ram Sharma. Wikipedia credits him with facilitating the dialogue between Gen Z protest leaders and the political leadership in September 2025." vs 'Transition, 10-14 Sept 2025: army chief who opened talks with Gen Z representatives from the night of 9 Sept, told embassy attaches it was not a coup, and attended the Friday meeting at Sheetal Niwas; reportedly warned an emergency might be declared if no government was in place by the evening of 12 Sept.' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
- person:kp-sharma-oli.profile: "Chairman of CPN-UML (2014-2018; again from 2021). Prime Minister three times: 12 Oct 2015-4 Aug 2016, 15 Feb 2018-13 Jul 2021 and 15 Jul 2024 to September 2025. He resigned on 9 September 2025 during the Gen Z protests; Wikipedia's biography gives 12 September 2025 as the end of the term, the date Sushila Karki took over. After the 5 March 2026 election (he lost Jhapa-5 to Balen Shah, per Wikipedia) he was detained on 28 March 2026 following the recommendation of the government commission on the protest deaths; the Supreme Court declined to release him and Ramesh Lekhak (reported 31 March 2026). The NHRC report held him primarily responsible for the rights violations (reported 27 May 2026)." vs 'Transition, 10-14 Sept 2025: resigned on 9 Sept (1:30 pm per the Kathmandu Post, 2:00 pm per Setopati), was kept under army protection at the Shivapuri staff college, wrote to "Dear Gen Z kids" on 10 Sept that he had not left the country, and left army protection on 18 Sept for a rented house in the Gundu area of Bhaktapur.' (transition-10-14-sept.json)
